falsifiers: If either interaction is zero/negative, evidence for the corresponding routing amplification is absent; both zero/negative rejects the predicted complementarity for this operational implementation. A curvature gain equally large in both routes supports ordered information without task-routing interaction.

If QS fails to exceed DS and SS, ordered curvature is unsupported in shared routing. If QT still exceeds both task replacements, this supports a route-dependent local observation only, not a general statement that shared representations cannot use order.

If routing main effects improve every replacement equally, do not attribute that main effect to curvature. If arbitrary scrambled information matches quadratic in both routes, the ordered-curvature explanation is weakened.
